--- Page 1 (Beckerman_32a) --- Dear Jack, We have 2 of your letters that we received this week to answer now - of 6*14/1 Jan. We were glad to hear that all is still going along so well. In the past week things have run the usual course here, with almost daily mail to brighten the picture. Abe, as you know is getting along as well as can be. This is of course very far fetched but we were wondering if there is any chance in the near or far future of going traveling again- perhaps to the Philippines? Of course you can see the connection but we because you can't make your own plans in the army. Well, we'll credit that expedition among the hopefuls. We have some good news about sending records. The postal clerk at the 23rd office may have been temperamental or something but he said it would be permissible to ship records or anything else of size, as long as --- Page 2 (Beckerman_32b) --- It is something that will 'contribute toward raising the poldurs or sailors morale'. Records can definitely be in- terpreted as coming under this category so it should be O.K. A specific request for them with a little morale building story would assure their acceptance. So name the number and well send the syncopation. - Macy's does a superb job packing! He can understand why everyone is so mad about those overdue packages - they were promised to arrive for Christmas. There are 5 small ones in all that we've sent; 2 containing film; developing paper, drugstore items, and some candied fruit that may just be good enough to look at when it arrives. I wish it all 'Bon Voyage' and quick. There's one thing we'd like to ask you for; - a good picture of yourself. The one we have on the dresser from back in the days of Camp Craft is a bit outdated; in uniform for one thing. Leave it to a photographer or your camera if you wish.
